method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.source: CDC Blood glucose monitoring and insulin administration
sourceChecks.supports: Single-person insulin pens/fingerstick devices; professional meters with manufacturer-directed cleaning/disinfection after every shared use; clean supplies separated from used equipment. Supports151–154.
Replace damp/loose/soiled dressings; gauze for oozing; protect catheter and connections with impermeable cover for showering. Supports161–162/165.

items.assessment: Patient-specific pen restriction is correct despite new needle and same insulin; alternatives test plausible product/cleaning/shortage misconceptions. CDC primary guidance confirms.
Internal blood-contamination key is correct, but always-inaccurate and visible-bleeding-only statements are easy absolutes; this is foundation recognition.
issues: Internal blood-contamination key is correct, but always-inaccurate and visible-bleeding-only statements are easy absolutes; this is foundation recognition.
proposedChanges: Compare possible reasons in parallel terms: retained blood in reusable device, test-strip calibration differences, different skin thickness, and lancet depth setting. Explain actual infection mechanism and label foundation or make choice of corrective workflow applied.

items.assessment: Professional shared-use meter with validated processing is correct. Different strip brand is unrelated; omitted instructions directly advertise failure.
issues: Professional shared-use meter with validated processing is correct. Different strip brand is unrelated; omitted instructions directly advertise failure.
proposedChanges: Compare candidate meters using meaningful attributes: professional shared-use design with validated disinfection, personal meter with disposable cover, personal meter with easy-clean casing, and meter with antimicrobial surface but no validated shared-use process. Keep lengths parallel and avoid cueing omissions in option wording.

items.assessment: Hand hygiene, meter processing and supply separation are sound; storing used lancets beside strips is too conspicuous.
issues: Hand hygiene, meter processing and supply separation are sound; storing used lancets beside strips is too conspicuous.
proposedChanges: Replace with a realistic workflow error such as carrying unused test strips and the used meter in the same uniform pocket, or cleaning shared meter at the end of the round. Consider five choices with varied key count.

items.assessment: Both hands and handle require correction, but paper covering and glove wiping are weak alternatives.
issues: Both hands and handle require correction, but paper covering and glove wiping are weak alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare glove removal/hand hygiene plus handle disinfection, glove change then scheduled cart cleaning, disinfecting handle while wearing current gloves then continuing, and assigning cart to current client. Explain the full transmission chain; shorten key.

items.assessment: Patient-area exposure should trigger dedicated use/disposal under injection policy, but same-diagnosis sharing is filler.
issues: Patient-area exposure should trigger dedicated use/disposal under injection policy, but same-diagnosis sharing is filler.
proposedChanges: Compare dedicated use for current client, return after stopper disinfection, return if vial remained capped, and use within a shortened beyond-use time. Cite specific injection-safety guidance for multidose vials in immediate treatment areas.

items.assessment: Overnight room-temperature chicken and reliance on smell create a concrete food-safety misconception. Discarding is defensible; reheating/tasting/late refrigeration are realistic unsafe remedies.
Discarding contaminated salad and correcting storage is sound, but all alternatives use only plus unrelated properties.
issues: Discarding contaminated salad and correcting storage is sound, but all alternatives use only plus unrelated properties.
proposedChanges: Compare discarding salad and storing raw poultry below ready-to-eat food, rinsing salad and changing shelves, removing the visibly affected leaves, and chilling both foods more quickly. Keep options comparable.

items.assessment: Correct safe-food principles, but generic SATA repeats157/158 with the same tasting misconception and no distinctive older-adult cues.
issues: Correct safe-food principles, but generic SATA repeats157/158 with the same tasting misconception and no distinctive older-adult cues.
proposedChanges: Create a preparation sequence with specific raw-food utensil reuse, prompt divided-container refrigeration, and handwashing steps; ask which steps need correction or are safe. Add a distinct practical decision and vary key positions/count.

items.assessment: Milk protein versus lactose distinction is useful and key is correct. Test bite is an implausible nurse action for documented severe allergy.
issues: Milk protein versus lactose distinction is useful and key is correct. Test bite is an implausible nurse action for documented severe allergy.
proposedChanges: Replace test bite with requesting the usual lactose-free substitution or checking carbohydrate content; preferably compare plausible tray-verification approaches, with ingredient confirmation decisive. Add a direct milk-allergy source.

items.assessment: Damp dressing replacement is primary-source supported. Dry towel over a central-line dressing is a weak alternative.
issues: Damp dressing replacement is primary-source supported. Dry towel over a central-line dressing is a weak alternative.
proposedChanges: Replace towel option with reinforcing with an additional transparent dressing. Retain scheduled-delay and tape-edge misconceptions; key can simply say replace dressing aseptically now.

items.assessment: Gauze during oozing is supported by CDC. Despite-accumulating-fluid, previous-damp and nonsterile qualifiers make all nonkeys self-disqualifying.
issues: Gauze during oozing is supported by CDC. Despite-accumulating-fluid, previous-damp and nonsterile qualifiers make all nonkeys self-disqualifying.
proposedChanges: Compare sterile gauze, transparent semipermeable film, chlorhexidine-impregnated transparent dressing, and leaving current intact film until the routine change. Put the oozing cue in stem and explain why absorbency is preferred; avoid unqualified advanced dressing claims.

items.assessment: Completing labelled antiseptic/drying process is correct, but blowing and touching the connector are weak.
issues: Completing labelled antiseptic/drying process is correct, but blowing and touching the connector are weak.
proposedChanges: Compare allowing specified drying, wiping excess antiseptic with sterile gauze, connecting while wet, and repeating scrub with a different antiseptic. Explain drying/contact requirements without inventing a universal duration.

items.assessment: Review necessity/removal/documentation is correct; indefinitely for convenience is a conspicuous nonkey.
issues: Review necessity/removal/documentation is correct; indefinitely for convenience is a conspicuous nonkey.
proposedChanges: Use a stable client now taking oral treatment with no anticipated IV need; compare concrete removal, site assessment, continuing a saline lock until discharge, and documenting plan. Avoid indefinitely and vary pattern.

items.assessment: Protecting site and connections for showering is correct and source-supported. Warm tap-water disinfection is cartoon wrong.
issues: Protecting site and connections for showering is correct and source-supported. Warm tap-water disinfection is cartoon wrong.
proposedChanges: Compare an impermeable cover for site and connections, covering insertion dressing alone, disconnecting infusion and leaving capped connector exposed, and planning an immediate dressing change after shower. Explain prevention and device-specific protocol.

items.assessment: Clean-to-dirty sequence with separate supplies is appropriate, but explicit same-gloves and one-set-for-same-client cues make the key uniquely comprehensive.
issues: Clean-to-dirty sequence with separate supplies is appropriate, but explicit same-gloves and one-set-for-same-client cues make the key uniquely comprehensive.
proposedChanges: Describe competing care sequences in parallel, with glove/hand hygiene performed in each where appropriate; distinguish clean-to-dirty sequencing and reuse of a cleansing container. Ensure any alternative dirty-first with full aseptic reset is not incorrectly called universally unsafe.

items.assessment: Terminal processing must be complete, but odour and belongings are filler.
issues: Terminal processing must be complete, but odour and belongings are filler.
proposedChanges: Compare confirming completed terminal-cleaning checklist, changing linens, disinfecting bed rails alone, and allowing a stated vacancy interval. If introducing a pathogen-specific vacancy requirement, source-check it; infectious diarrhoea generally needs actual cleaning, not waiting.

items.assessment: Spore-active product is correct but strongest smell, hand antiseptic, fastest drying are implausible selection criteria.
issues: Spore-active product is correct but strongest smell, hand antiseptic, fastest drying are implausible selection criteria.
proposedChanges: Compare products with concrete label claims: bactericidal general-purpose product, labelled sporicidal product, alcohol-based surface wipe, and neutral detergent. Label foundation if it remains direct product-claim recognition.

items.assessment: Soil removal/contact time/compatibility are correct but fragrance is filler in a professional cleaning audit.
issues: Soil removal/contact time/compatibility are correct but fragrance is filler in a professional cleaning audit.
proposedChanges: Replace fragrance with whether surface is wiped dry immediately after application, or a realistic log-only compliance measure. Make this a concrete observed workflow and avoid the repeated three-correct pattern.

items.assessment: Compatible processing plus hand hygiene is correct; pillow placement and same glove all day are weak.
issues: Compatible processing plus hand hygiene is correct; pillow placement and same glove all day are weak.
proposedChanges: Compare processing between indicated uses, applying a disposable cover changed daily, cleaning at shift end, and using a dedicated stylus carried room to room. Explain touch transfer and device compatibility.

items.assessment: Equipment/linen turnover is correct, but spraying linen and no-processing-for-similar-client are weak.
issues: Equipment/linen turnover is correct, but spraying linen and no-processing-for-similar-client are weak.
proposedChanges: Compare replacing linens plus equipment processing, replacing linens and visible-soil spot cleaning, processing mattress but retaining clean-looking linen, and covering used surface with a disposable sheet. Keep correct option concise.

items.assessment: Symptomatic visitor restriction/alternative support is appropriate. Asking visitor to conceal symptoms is absurd.
issues: Symptomatic visitor restriction/alternative support is appropriate. Asking visitor to conceal symptoms is absurd.
proposedChanges: Compare arranging remote contact under screening guidance, offering a mask for a brief bedside visit, keeping visitor across the room, and scheduling the visit after an antipyretic. State elective social visit and vulnerable client; account for local exceptions if necessary.

items.assessment: Engineering failure needs coordinated urgent response; open-door equalization and permanent standard-room transfer are weak. Challenge label is unsupported by the simple stem.
issues: Engineering failure needs coordinated urgent response; open-door equalization and permanent standard-room transfer are weak. Challenge label is unsupported by the simple stem.
proposedChanges: Compare keeping door closed and activating facilities/IPAC pathway, moving to the nearest private room, increasing portable fan airflow, and resetting alarm after checking door seal. Add relevant symptoms/placement constraints if retaining challenge; avoid suggesting untrained engineering adjustments.

items.assessment: Positive-pressure protective environment is a meaningful technical misconception among otherwise appropriate airborne preparations. Placement, communication and supplies are valid; rationale correctly distinguishes pressure direction.
Immediate cleaning and supportive feedback are right, but annual delay and finishing other rooms are implausible.
issues: Immediate cleaning and supportive feedback are right, but annual delay and finishing other rooms are implausible.
proposedChanges: Compare prompting immediate cleaning, applying fresh gloves, reporting breach after current task, and arranging technique retraining at next huddle. Explain current contamination requires correction before further contact; put later learning in rationale.
